summary: Session-transport series is well-engineered and internally consistent with its own spec (fail-closed MCP parsing, correct process-group reaping, honest security posture docs, layered decorrelation enforcement, zero regressions in the existing 60-test suite). Blocked for two reasons: (1) the spec own live-acceptance step (Task 11 demo) was never executed, so the real codex mcp-server tool and property schema is unverified against a live install; (2) main has independently evolved past the hard-mode adapter architecture this series depends on (worker-run.sh is now a stub on main, audit-run.sh no longer sources adapters, adapters directory does not exist on main), so no simple merge path exists.

findings.summary: main worker-run.sh is a stub (containerized worker not shipped) and main audit-run.sh no longer sources the adapters directory, which does not exist on main at all; a cherry-pick or patch-apply of this series will conflict on every hunk touching worker-run.sh, audit-run.sh, and lib/common.sh, and if force-applied would resurrect a deprecated hard-mode path main intentionally stubbed out

the codex mcp-server tool name and property schema (codex/codex-reply, prompt/cwd/sandbox/approval-policy/threadId) were never confirmed against a live installed server; the plan explicitly defers this to the Task 11 live demo, which was never executed (docs/demo-log.md absent, all 46 plan checkboxes unchecked)

mcp-mode timeout enforcement relies solely on the adapter-internal timeout (group_timeout for claude/grok, --timeout-sec in mcp-session.py for codex) with no outer watchdog in worker-run.sh, unlike the container path which wraps an additional outer timeout around the whole invocation

zero automated bats coverage was added for approximately 1900 new lines (mcp-session.py, adapter session functions, worker-run/audit-run transport branches); spec-authorized (decision D6) but leaves no regression guard for future changes
all 46 task checkboxes remain unchecked despite Tasks 1-10 being functionally complete per commit history, unlike the prior v1 plan doc which was re-marked complete after its dogfood run
